definitions.explanation: A metal chisel used for cutting or shaping metal, stone, or concrete. Unlike woodworking chisels, it is made entirely of hardened steel and struck with a hammer.

examples.japanese: たがねとハンマーで{金属|きんぞく}を{切|き}る。
examples.english: I cut metal with a cold chisel and hammer.

examples.japanese: コンクリートをたがねで{削|けず}った。
examples.english: I chipped away the concrete with a cold chisel.

examples.japanese: {錆|さ}びた{釘|くぎ}をたがねで{叩|たた}き{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I knocked out the rusty nail with a cold chisel.

notes:
KANJI WRITING:
・{鏨|たがね} (rarely used)
・Usually written in hiragana

DIFFERENCE FROM WOOD CHISEL:
・のみ (wood chisel) - has wooden handle, used on wood
・たがね (cold chisel) - all metal, used on metal/stone/concrete

TYPES:
・{平|ひら}たがね (flat cold chisel)
・{先|さき}たがね (point chisel)
・センターポンチ (center punch - for marking)

RELATED TOOLS:
・のみ (wood chisel)
・ハンマー/{金槌|かなづち} (hammer)
・{万力|まんりき} (vise)
・グラインダー (grinder)

COLLOCATIONS:
・たがねを{打|う}つ (to strike a cold chisel)
・たがねで{切|き}る (to cut with a cold chisel)
・たがねで{割|わ}る (to split with a cold chisel)
